approach:
Point OLY-B-O1-01 in docs/spec.toml at the existing `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range` (rule M6). Its single-line measure names the tests and ends `status: not shown`. Three tests show it. (a) New crates/athena-gate/tests/bootstrap_requirement.rs parses TOML with the `toml` crate, which is already a normal dependency of athena-gate. A pure `check_entry(&str)` validates the entry's fields. One test runs it on the real docs/spec.toml (expects Ok), one on a literal base-entry fixture wrapped in `[[requirement]]` (expects Err), and one drives the real `bootstrap_range` in a temp repo through Open then ClosedThrough. (b) A new in-source test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, modelled on `oly_b_set_04_no_longer_appears_in_the_spec_gap_list`, runs the real gap rule (`parse_spec`, `measure_problem`, `spec_gaps`) on the real spec. This is the rule that queues the request. It fails on the base tree. (c) The existing in-source rule-M6 test is the evidence that the gate refuses a bootstrap commit after the range closes. The plan also adds a doc-comment line on `bootstrap_range`, a CHANGELOG bullet and one line in xtask/shard-timings.txt. The gate's behavior does not change.

**Reading versus brief.** The accepted reading's deliverables name a gate test file, but its Code survey, Existing code and Consumers lines do not name hestia.rs or xtask/shard-timings.txt. The brief's own "Files: docs/spec.toml, crates/" scope covers hestia.rs. shard-timings.txt is needed only because of the new test file (see decision 4).

decisions.choice: Mechanism is the existing `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range` (rule M6). The measure says 'v0 stays small' is not mechanically enforced and ends `status: not shown`.
decisions.reason: invariant.rs:60-79 defines the range. invariant.rs:175-197 refuses `Athena-Job: bootstrap` after the outcome record closes it. That mechanises 'recorded as such, the only work outside Athena'. The user accepted this reading. `measure_problem` (hestia.rs:1219-1239) accepts any measure whose last `status:` label starts with `not shown`, and xtask/tests/spec.rs needs only the `status: <label>` ending. The measure must stay on one line and contain `status:` exactly once, at the end, because `measure_label` uses `rsplit_once` (hestia.rs:1212).

rejected.option: Add a size limit for v0
rejected.why: Out of scope. No threshold is defined.

rejected.option: Add an `athena status` label such as `status: bootstrap`
rejected.why: Out of scope. It would change STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS. `athena status` already prints a `bootstrap` line from bootstrap_view (status.rs:1184), but the plan adds no label.

decisions.choice: Answers finding 2: add an athena-core in-source test `oly_b_o1_01_no_longer_appears_in_the_spec_gap_list` in the tests module of crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, right after `oly_b_set_04_no_longer_appears_in_the_spec_gap_list` (hestia.rs:4315-4334). It parses `include_str!("../../../docs/spec.toml")` with `parse_spec`. It finds OLY-B-O1-01 and asserts `measure_problem(&r.measure) == None`, mechanism != "none", mechanism contains `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range`, and owner == "Athena". It asserts that `spec_gaps(&requirements)` has no entry with that id. It asserts that a clone with mechanism "none" gives exactly one gap with `no_mechanism`. The measure names it, and the verifier runs `cargo test -p athena-core oly_b_o1_01`.
decisions.reason: `spec_gaps` (hestia.rs:1291-1308) is the code that re-queues 'Give requirement ... a mechanism' and fills the `athena status` spec_gaps. athena-gate cannot reach athena-core (crate reach: gate deps data git score), so only an athena-core test can run the real rule on the real entry. An in-source test needs no new test unit and no shard-timings line. The pattern is the existing one (hestia.rs:4315, status.rs:1631-1656). On the base tree this test fails, because mechanism is "none" and the entry is a gap. That is a real fails-without for the production rule.

rejected.option: Make a new crates/athena-core/tests/*.rs integration test
rejected.why: It adds a test unit and so another shard-timings line, and the same coverage is available in-source.

rejected.option: Have the gate test re-implement the gap rule
rejected.why: This was the critic's finding. A re-implementation is not the production rule, and gate cannot depend on core.

decisions.choice: Answers finding 3: `check_entry(text: &str) -> Result<(), String>` in the gate test parses with `toml::from_str` into `struct Doc { #[serde(default)] requirement: Vec<Req> }` and `struct Req { #[serde(default)] id/mechanism/owner/measure: String }`. Serde ignores the other fields. It finds the entry whose id is `OLY-B-O1-01` and checks the fields. Mechanism must not be blank or "none" (case-insensitive), and must contain `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range`. Owner must equal "Athena". The measure, trimmed, must end with `status: not shown`, contain `bootstrap`, and contain `status:` once. The base fixture is wrapped as `[[requirement]]` plus the entry lines.
decisions.reason: Parsing fields is robust against quoting style, escapes and line layout. The `toml` crate is a normal dependency of athena-gate (Cargo.toml:20), and `serde` is one too (line 16), so the integration test reaches both and Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock stay unchanged. The real spec is about 200 KB of valid TOML that hestia::parse_spec already parses.

rejected.option: Slice raw text by `id = ` and `[[requirement]]` and match `measure = ` lines
rejected.why: A literal string or an escaped quote would defeat the substring checks, and the line ends with a closing quote.

rejected.option: Parse with toml_edit as hestia does
rejected.why: toml_edit is not a dependency of athena-gate, and the plain `toml` crate is.

decisions.choice: Keep the Open/ClosedThrough range test in the gate test file, but state plainly that criterion 3 rests on existing evidence. The refusal of a late `Athena-Job: bootstrap` commit is shown by the existing in-source test `bootstrap_commits_pass_while_the_range_is_open_and_not_after` (invariant.rs:1102-1122). The assert at invariant.rs:1121 is the evidence. The new range test calls the unchanged `bootstrap_range` and passes on the base tree. It is a direct check that the outcome record closes the range, and it is not counted for criterion 2.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. The brief lists a gate test file, and the range test is cheap. Running the full `check` from an integration test needs the testkit as a dev-dependency, which would change Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock for nothing the in-source test does not already cover.

rejected.why: The `bootstrap` filter would then reach only the in-source test, and a direct range check is cheap.

rejected.option: Add a testkit dev-dependency to run `check` in the integration test
rejected.why: This would change Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock for coverage that already exists.

decisions.choice: Answers finding 1: keep the one-line xtask/shard-timings.txt change: add `athena-gate --test bootstrap_requirement 5.00` after `athena-gate --lib 10.00` (line 59). Label it an estimate in the changelog.
decisions.reason: The brief requires the new file crates/athena-gate/tests/bootstrap_requirement.rs, and it is a new workspace test unit. `checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit` (xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:410-421) asserts that the set of timed units equals the oracle, so the full test would fail without the line. The file is a data file, not a governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, lint config). Precedent: `athena-core --test model_roster 5.00` (line 53). The `--test` unit sorts after `--lib`.

rejected.why: The brief lists the tests file as a deliverable, and the accepted reading says a new test file.

steps: Edit docs/spec.toml at OLY-B-O1-01 (line 2163). Create crates/athena-gate/tests/bootstrap_requirement.rs. Add `repo_file` as in model_roster.rs:11-16 and `check_entry(text: &str) -> Result<(), String>`, which parses with `toml::from_str` into Doc/Req structs (`#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]`, `#[serde(default)]` on all fields). It finds id OLY-B-O1-01 and rejects: mechanism blank or "none"; mechanism without `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range`; owner != "Athena"; a measure that, trimmed, does not end `status: not shown`, does not contain `bootstrap`, or has `status:` more than once. Tests: `spec_entry_names_the_bootstrap_range_gate` runs it on repo_file("docs/spec.toml") and asserts Ok. `base_entry_is_rejected` runs it on a literal `[[requirement]]` fixture copied from the base entry (mechanism none, measure 'The spec gap list; status: requirement') and asserts Err mentioning the mechanism. `bootstrap_range_is_open_then_closed_by_the_outcome_record` makes a tempdir, runs `Git::isolated`, `git init -q -b main`, writes a file and commits it, and asserts `bootstrap_range(&git, "HEAD")` is `BootstrapRange::Open`. It then writes records/jobs/bootstrap/outcome.json (JSON copied from invariant.rs:1109 with `through_commit` set to the first commit id), commits it, and asserts `ClosedThrough(<id>)`.

Add the in-source test `oly_b_o1_01_no_longer_appears_in_the_spec_gap_list` in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs tests, after hestia.rs:4334. Parse the real spec with `parse_spec(include_str!("../../../docs/spec.toml"))`, find the id with `.expect`, and assert mechanism != "none", mechanism contains `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range`, owner == "Athena" and `measure_problem(&r.measure) == None`. Assert that `spec_gaps(&requirements)` has no gap with that id. Clone the entry with mechanism "none" and assert `spec_gaps(&[without])` has length 1 with `no_mechanism` true.

Add `athena-gate --test bootstrap_requirement 5.00` to xtask/shard-timings.txt directly after `athena-gate --lib 10.00` (line 59), keeping the sorted order.

Add a first bullet under [Unreleased] / Added in CHANGELOG.md, in the style of the OLY-B-SET-02 entry (CHANGELOG.md:26-32). It says: OLY-B-O1-01 now has a mechanism, `bootstrap_range` (rule M6); the measure is `status: not shown` and names the gate and hestia tests; 'v0 stays small' stays prose; the gate and the records are unchanged; the new test file is registered in xtask/shard-timings.txt with a 5.00 s estimate.

Run `cargo fmt --all`. Then run `cargo test -p athena-gate`, `cargo test -p athena-core oly_b_o1_01`, `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, to cover the xtask spec test, the shard-timings check and the policy scans over the new text.

risks.risk: The measure is parsed with `rsplit_once("status:")` (hestia.rs:1212, xtask spec.rs:194-213). A second `status:` or a multi-line measure would break the ending.
risks.mitigation: Write the measure on one line with `status:` only once, at the end. `check_entry` enforces the same rule on the real entry, and the xtask spec test and the hestia test run it again.

risks.risk: The literal base-entry fixture in `base_entry_is_rejected` could drift from the real spec.
risks.mitigation: It is a fixed copy of the base entry, kept only to show that the checker rejects mechanism "none". It does not read docs/spec.toml, so later spec edits cannot break it.

risks.risk: The temp-repo test needs a git binary and identity settings in the checks' environment.
risks.mitigation: `Git::isolated` sets author, committer and gpgsign=false, the same setup as the in-source helpers (gate/src/lib.rs:396-418). The test runs `git init -q -b main` itself.

risks.risk: The outcome JSON in the range test drifts from the `athena.outcome/1` schema, so parsing fails and `ClosedThrough` carries an empty id.
risks.mitigation: Copy the JSON from the string at invariant.rs:1109, which the existing test already parses, and assert `ClosedThrough(id)` with the real commit id.

risks.risk: The 5.00 s timing is an estimate and could skew shard balance slightly.
risks.mitigation: The changelog bullet labels it an estimate. Balance does not affect correctness, and the file can be refreshed with `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings`.

risks.risk: The new hestia test is in a large file, and a future spec edit that supersedes OLY-B-O1-01 would break `.unwrap()` on a missing id or the active-state assumption.
risks.mitigation: Use `.expect("OLY-B-O1-01 is in the spec")`, as in status.rs:1637, and keep it independent of any other entry. Superseding the requirement should also drop the test.

risks.risk: 'v0 stays small' is not enforced, so the requirement is only partly mechanised.
risks.mitigation: The measure says so and ends `status: not shown`. The changelog bullet repeats it.

risks.risk: `cargo fmt --all --check` fails on the new files.
risks.mitigation: Step 7 runs `cargo fmt --all` before the checks.
